narrative.overview:
Design Scheduling is a console you glance at between other work: on a second monitor beside SolidWorks, snapped beside File Explorer, or pulled out on a phone on the workshop floor. Like a wheelhouse at night it is dark and quiet at rest, and the only things that light up are the things that need you. A job waiting on someone glows amber, work ready for checking glows violet, a send-back glows red. Everything else stays in greys, so a status change is noticed the moment the eye lands on the page.

The system belongs to the Stella family: the production board, material ordering and the workshop drawings app.

- **Shared with the family:** the same Black Night ground, Shadow Grey surfaces, Upsdell Red primary action, and the Burning Star Red rule under the header. - **Different:** the density. This is a working list, not a printed board. Rows are tight, labels are small uppercase captions, and numbers line up. - **Friz Quadrata** names places (the app, each view, each section). The body face does everything you read in a row or act on.

Controls are **quiet and exact**: hairline borders, modest 8px corners, outlined secondary actions, and one filled red button at most per view. Surfaces are flat and told apart by tone. Only things that float over the page cast a shadow: the task panel, the phone sheet, menus and toasts. Motion exists only to show that something changed state.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, calm and greyscale at rest. Hue is reserved for signals.
Dense rows (44px) on a 4/8px rhythm, readable at half-screen width.
Friz Quadrata for place names; the body face for everything actionable.
Flat surfaces with tonal layers; shadows only on floating layers.
One filled primary action per view, in Upsdell Red.
A light **Workshop** theme exists for bright rooms. It swaps variables only (`css/themes.css`).

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Colour at rest is greyscale. Hue appears only when it says something: a status, a category dot, a count, or the single primary action. If a coloured element carries no meaning, it goes grey.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: - Upsdell Red fills at most one button per view. - Burning Star Red is for lines and markers (header rule, active tab, focus, counts), never a filled area larger than a count bubble.

rules.name: The Dot-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Categories are a dot and, at most, a thin rule. They never fill a row, card or chip, so they can never be mistaken for a status.

rules.name: The Word-With-Colour Rule
rules.body: Status colour always travels with its word ("Waiting", "Ready for check"). Colour alone never carries the meaning.

rules.name: The Friz-for-Places Rule
rules.body: - Friz Quadrata names where you are: the app, the view, the section. - Anything you can click, edit or scan in a row is set in the body face. - Never set a job or task title in Friz.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Counts, ages and dates use tabular figures, so columns of numbers line up and don't jitter as they change.

rules.name: The 16px Input Rule
rules.body: On phone widths, text inputs are 16px, so iOS never zooms the page on focus.

rules.name: The Half-Screen Rule
rules.body: Every view is designed and checked at about 900px wide (snapped beside CAD), as well as at 375px and full desktop. Nothing important may depend on width above 1100px.

rules.name: The Glance Rule
rules.body: A row's status, owner and age are readable without hovering, expanding or opening anything.

rules.name: The Give-Way Rule
rules.body: When a row runs short of room, nothing leaves its box. Things give way in a fixed order: 1. touch targets narrow first, never below the control as drawn; 2. then text ends in an ellipsis, with the whole words kept in the accessible name or menu; 3. or a fact moves to a second place that has room (a tile's age drops to its foot on phones).

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing at rest casts a shadow. Cards, tiles and rows are flat. A shadow means "this is above the page and will go away".

dos: **Do** keep the screen greyscale at rest and let the status hues carry meaning (the Signal Rule).
**Do** write the status word inside every status pill. Colour is never the only signal.
**Do** keep job and task rows at 44px. Use tabular figures for every count, age and date.
**Do** check every view at 375px, about 900px (half-screen) and full desktop before calling it done.
**Do** use the Floating panel shadow only on layers that float and dismiss: panel, sheet, menu, popover, toast.
**Do** show focus as the 2px Burning Star Red ring, offset 2px, on every interactive element.
**Do** set folder paths and revisions in the mono face.
**Do** let a crowded row give way in order: touch targets first, then an ellipsis, or move a fact to a second place (the Give-Way Rule). Nothing pokes out of its tile.
**Do** put tiles on a surface one tone away from their own. Inside the grey panel, children sit on the ground.
**Do** say load errors and refusals in plain words, with what to do next, and keep what someone typed when a post is refused.
donts: **Don't** change the Stella tokens in `css/style.css` or the Friz Quadrata headings without the owner's approval.
**Don't** fill more than one button per view with Upsdell Red. Never fill an area with Burning Star Red beyond a count bubble.
**Don't** fill rows, cards or chips with category colour. Categories are dots.
**Don't** put shadows on cards, tiles or rows at rest.
**Don't** hide an action behind hover or right-click alone. Every action needs a visible, touchable control.
**Don't** animate anything that isn't a change of state, and never on page load.
**Don't** set job or task titles in Friz Quadrata. Don't ship the licensed font files.
**Don't** show raw backend errors ("Missing or insufficient permissions") to anyone.
**Don't** fill Approve red where several checks share a page. On check tiles it is outlined.
